author: philly leader
title: Eagles agree to terms with Elijah Moore on one-year contract
text:
The Philadelphia Eagles announced on Mar. 25 that they have agreed to terms with wide receiver Elijah Moore on a one-year contract.
The move brings another experienced player into the Eagles’ wide receiver group as the team continues to shape its roster for the upcoming season. The Eagles operate as a professional American football team in the National Football League, according to the official website.
Moore was drafted by the New York Jets in 2021 after playing at Ole Miss, where he earned first-team All-American honors and set a school record for receiving yards in a season. During his two years with the Jets, Moore caught 80 passes for 984 yards and six touchdowns over 27 games. He was then traded to the Cleveland Browns, where he saw increased usage and averaged nearly 600 receiving yards per season across back-to-back campaigns. In 2025, Moore signed with the Buffalo Bills but was waived later that year before joining the Denver Broncos’ practice squad.
Moore is known for his speed, having run a 4.35-second 40-yard dash at his Pro Day before being selected No. 34 overall by New York. His addition gives depth to an Eagles wide receiver room that already includes A.J. Brown, DeVonta Smith, Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper, Britain Covey, Danny Gray, Quez Watkins, and Johnny Wilson. Notably, Moore and A.J. Brown played together at Ole Miss for one season.
